title: Lesson 6: The Biblical Storyline
description: On the road to Emmaus, Jesus showed two discouraged friends that the whole Bible was about Him. This lesson traces that one story in four movements, Creation, Fall, Redemption, and Restoration, and helps you see where your own life fits.

blocks.text: In the last lesson you got the map: 66 books on the shelves of one library. Now comes the road trip. You are going to follow the one line that runs through the whole library, from creation to new creation, and the best guide for that trip is Jesus Himself.

blocks.title: The Road to Emmaus
blocks.text:
On the Sunday Jesus rose from the dead, two of His followers were walking home from Jerusalem to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles away. They were talking about everything that had happened: the trial, the cross, the tomb. A stranger came alongside and asked what they were discussing, and they stood still in the road, looking sad.

They told Him about Jesus, a prophet mighty in deed and word, and how the leaders had handed Him over to be crucified. Then came the saddest words in the story: "But we had hoped that he was the one to redeem Israel" (Luke 24:21). As far as they could tell, the story had ended at the cross.

The stranger was Jesus, but "their eyes were kept from recognizing him" (Luke 24:16). First He opened the Scriptures:

"And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself." (Luke 24:27)

Imagine that seven-mile walk, with Jesus tracing the line from the garden to the cross. That evening at the table, He took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, and suddenly they knew Him. Then He vanished from their sight, and they said to each other, "Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked to us on the road, while he opened to us the Scriptures?" (Luke 24:32)

They got up that same hour and went back to Jerusalem. The story had not ended at the cross. It had turned there.

Those two disciples knew the facts, but they could not see the shape. Jesus showed them that the cross was the turning point, not the end, and that the whole Bible was about Him. The whole Bible is one story, Creation, Fall, Redemption, and Restoration, and Jesus is at the center of it.
6.1 - The disciples said, "We had hoped." Where does your own story feel stuck in the middle right now?
One Story in Four Movements

blocks.alt: A four-part sketch sequence showing the biblical story line from creation in a garden, to the fall, to redemption at the cross, to restoration in a renewed kingdom

blocks.text: The Bible opens in a garden, and the line of the story begins with God. He made the heavens and the earth, filled the world with beauty, and placed Adam and Eve at the center of it as His image-bearers. Even here Jesus is at the center, because "all things were created through him and for him" (Colossians 1:16). This is Creation: everything good, everything whole, everything under the loving rule of God.

Then the serpent lied. He told them they could be like God without trusting God, and they believed him. Sin entered the world, and the garden became a place of hiding. Their relationship with God was fractured, and death entered what God had made alive. This is the Fall: sin breaking what God made good.

But God did not abandon His world. Even in the garden, He promised that one day a Son would come to crush the serpent. At the cross, Jesus took the curse of sin. At the empty tomb, He defeated death. This is Redemption: God coming to rescue what people could never repair on their own.

And the story is not over. Jesus is coming again to make all things new. The Bible that begins in a garden ends in a renewed creation, where God dwells with His people and every tear is wiped away. This is Restoration: everything broken made whole again forever.

The line begins with what God made good, drops when sin breaks the world, turns at the cross, and rises toward the day God makes all things new. Trace that line below through the big story, several smaller stories, and your own life.
The voice from the throne in the very last book of the Bible names the shape of the whole storyline in seven words.
Behold, I am making all things new.
6.2 - As you traced the four movements, where did you see Jesus most clearly?
Stories That Echo the Pattern

Many smaller stories inside the Bible echo this shape, like the same melody in a different key. Not every story fits neatly, and you do not need to force one into four boxes, but once you know the pattern you will notice it often.

1. Noah lived in a world God made good, but humanity corrupted it so deeply that God grieved He had made them. The flood was judgment, but the ark was rescue. When the waters receded, God set a rainbow in the sky and made a covenant to start again.

2. Joseph had his father's favor and dreams from God, until his brothers sold him into slavery and he spent years in an Egyptian prison. But God raised him from the pit to the palace, and Joseph lived to see God turn his brothers' evil into the saving of many lives.

3. Israel was God's chosen people, but they ended up enslaved in Egypt for four hundred years, crying out for a deliverer. God sent Moses, parted the sea, and led them out toward the land He had promised.

4. Paul was trained in Scripture and zealous for God, but his zeal was blind, and he hunted the very people God loved. Jesus met him on the road to Damascus. The man who tried to destroy the church spent the rest of his life building it.

Something good, something broken, God stepping in, and a new beginning. The echoes are not exact. Each rescue is a small preview of the great rescue Jesus came to bring. God writes rescue into chapter after chapter because He is the same Rescuer in every chapter.
6.3 - Which of these four stories do you connect with most, and why?
Your Story on the Line

And now, your story. You were made in the image of God, with dignity and worth that were settled before you ever did a single thing. Yet you were born into a broken world with a heart bent away from Him. That is where Creation and the Fall meet in every human life.

Redemption is not something you work up. It is Jesus coming for you. He lived the life you could not live, died for your sin, and rose again, and He invites you to turn from your sin and trust Him. If you have trusted Him, you have been found, forgiven, and given new life, and you are being restored day by day, not yet finished but already held. If you have not trusted Him yet, your story is not over. The same Jesus who walked beside two discouraged friends on that road is near to you, and today can be the day your story turns.

Followers of Jesus live between Redemption and Restoration. He has won the victory, but we are still waiting for Him to return and make all things new. Life holds both breathtaking goodness and deep pain, and neither gets the last word. The last word belongs to the One who said, "Behold, I am making all things new."

6.4 - This is your private rehearsal before you take it out into the week. In your own words, how would you explain the four-movement story of the Bible to a friend in two or three minutes, including where your own life fits on the line?
A Resource to Go Deeper

blocks.title: The Bible Project: The Story of the Bible
blocks.description: A short visual overview of how the entire Bible fits together as one unified story.

blocks.text: This Week's Practice

Take what you wrote in question 6.4 out into the week. First, walk one Bible story you already know through the four movements. Then find one real person this week, a family member, a coworker, or a friend over coffee, and tell them the storyline of the whole Bible in two or three minutes, the way you rehearsed it above. You will own the shape the moment you say it out loud.
Lesson 6 Review

Two travelers on the road to Emmaus thought their story had ended at the cross, until Jesus opened the Scriptures and showed them it was all about Him. You have walked the same road: Creation, Fall, Redemption, and Restoration. The whole Bible is one story, Creation, Fall, Redemption, and Restoration, and Jesus is at the center of it. Carry this one sentence with you: The same line runs through the Bible, and the same line runs through me.

You have the map, and you have taken the road trip. In the next lesson, you will learn the skill: a simple method for studying any passage on your own, building on the Three Discovery Questions from the Starting course.
